clue.text: Poor treatment is interrupting inspiration

indicators.note: something interrupting breaks into the middle of another word, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a muse is a source of artistic inspiration
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bad handling cuts into a moment of creative inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusing or handling something wrongly is treating it poorly, a direct synonym.

clue.text: High-class London woman spurning a musical

indicators.note: rejecting the letter, so it is taken out

parts.note: Mayfair is an exclusive district of London, so a lady from there is high-class

explanation.surface: A posh Londoner turns her nose up at a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: MAYFAIR is a wealthy London district; removing its A gives the show title.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lerner and Loewe stage show about Eliza Doolittle is a famous musical.

clue.text: Fish eggs cover river

indicators.note: the eggs cover the river, so that piece goes around it

parts.note: spat is the spawn of oysters and other shellfish

explanation.surface: Fish roe lies over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Spat, the spawn of oysters, is a less familiar word for eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The sprat is a small sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Spoke about King and showed surprise

indicators.note: the word for spoke is placed about the other piece, around it

parts.note: stated means said or spoke
R is for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone talked about the monarch and was taken aback.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to jump or flinch with surprise.

clue.text: Unwise: Penny, entering scoundrel's flat

indicators.note: these pieces entering the scoundrel go inside that word

parts.note: a cad is an ungentlemanly scoundrel
unwise means rash
P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: A reckless penniless rogue moves into an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an adjective but is the noun: somewhere to live.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash pad is slang for a place to sleep, usually a temporary flat or room.

clue.text: Latin dance? Curious dance, stopped halfway through

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or curious

indicators.note: the word is cut off at its midpoint, losing its back half

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A Latin American dance, oddly cut short in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a ballroom dance of Cuban, hence Latin American, origin.

clue.text: Country paths twisting round for example

indicators.note: the twisted paths go round the other piece
twisting rearranges the letters of the word

parts.note: lanes are narrow paths
EG abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Winding country lanes, as one instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisting' turns the paths word into SENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a nation in West Africa.

clue.text: No. good in love? Trying something else

indicators.note: the pieces go in the word for love

parts.note: passion is intense love
N abbreviates number

explanation.surface: Dismissing love as no good and moving to something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No. good' reads as a dismissive remark, but it supplies two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing on means declining one thing to move on to another option.

clue.text: Confusion on the radio for some time

indicators.note: broadcast speech is heard rather than read, so a word is chosen for its sound

parts.note: a daze is a state of confusion

explanation.surface: Muddle over the airwaves lasts a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Days stands for an unspecified period, as in in days gone by.

clue.text: Criminal later in court for decisive result

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go in the word for court

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: criminal means bad or wrong, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A felon later appears in court for a decisive outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges the given word to ATERL.
explanation.definitionFit: After the 1815 battle, the word means a final crushing defeat.

clue.text: Safety equipment (genuine article) imported by company

indicators.note: brought into the company, so these pieces go inside that word

parts.note: a firm is a business company
genuine means real
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A firm brings in authentic safety gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that warns of fire is a standard piece of safety kit in any building.

clue.text: Unpleasant way to block contrary vote

indicators.note: a piece put to block another word sits in its middle, obstructing it

parts.note: nay is a vote against a motion
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A spiteful tactic to obstruct an opposing ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpleasant and disagreeable are near synonyms for something horrid or mean.

clue.text: Very interested in the pub profits as well

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
taken as written
a bar is a pub or the room in one where drinks are served
profits are gain

explanation.surface: Someone keen on a pub's takings, and more besides.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in addition or besides, so it can replace also in a sentence.

clue.text: Prepared to deliver the money after a brief time

indicators.note: the money comes after the other pieces

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written
the ready is British slang for cash

explanation.surface: Ready to hand over the cash after a short wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ready' is British slang for available money.
explanation.definitionFit: At the ready means prepared for immediate use.

clue.text: Unpleasantly colourful cover wrapped round Volume I

indicators.note: the cover is wrapped round the other pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A garish jacket encloses the first volume of a set.
explanation.walkthrough: V and I go between LI and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid describes the bluish, bruised discolouration of skin, an ugly colouring.

clue.text: Seductress, female, married, being after one's blood?

parts.note: a vamp is a seductive woman
Iris is a female name

explanation.surface: A married temptress who wants your blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being after one's blood' plays on wanting revenge but describes a creature drinking blood.
explanation.definitionFit: The practice of sucking blood like the undead of legend is literally seeking blood.

clue.text: Story about maiden's dilemma not initially having prominence on stage

indicators.note: the story is placed about, that is around, the next piece

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a plight is a difficult predicament

explanation.surface: A tale about a young woman's predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' leaves LIGHT once the opening letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the public eye is a figurative sense taken from the stage lamp that lit the leading actor.

clue.text: Spoil one's period at sea?

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it
I is the Roman numeral one
a time is a period

explanation.surface: Ruining one's time at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime means relating to the sea, so things at sea are maritime.

clue.text: Lower the dignity of our behaviour

parts.note: to demean someone is to lower their dignity
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to degrade our conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's bearing and conduct is their manner, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Researcher taking speaker's view of record-keeper

indicators.note: the speaker's version is how the word sounds when spoken

parts.note: an annalist records events in yearly chronicles

explanation.surface: A scholar adopts an orator's perspective on a historian.
explanation.definitionFit: An analyst examines data and studies problems closely, as a researcher does.

clue.text: Drink suitable for horse?

parts.note: a fruity mixed drink that shares its name with a sturdy English breed of draught horse

explanation.surface: Asking what a horse might like to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Suffolk Punch is a heavy English working horse, so the drink's name suits it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed drink of spirits and fruit juice, also the name of a breed of horse.

clue.text: In part of London, United at first having many fans

indicators.note: the letter goes in the district name

parts.note: Poplar is a district of East London

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: In an East London district, the local United side once drew big crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular means widely liked, with many admirers.

clue.text: Plain wrap favoured by man in drag?

definitions.text: Plain wrap favoured by man in drag?

parts.words: Plain wrap favoured by man in drag?
parts.note: drag is a puff of smoke, so the man taking a drag wants a thin plain wrapping for tobacco, not a cross-dresser

explanation.surface: Asking what simple shawl a cross-dresser prefers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in drag' suggests a man dressed as a woman; here a drag is a draw on a roll-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin paper for rolling tobacco is a plain wrap used by a smoker.

clue.text: Track record a few trimmed

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: some means a few

explanation.surface: A racing track with a shortened record.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom Downs is a racecourse near London, home of the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is a racecourse, a track for horses.

clue.text: Nut about to be put in container

indicators.note: the abbreviation is put inside the container word

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure that contains animals
CA abbreviates circa, meaning about

explanation.surface: A nut is to be placed in a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'container' suggests a pan or can, but it is a pen for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is a nut from a hickory tree.

clue.text: Lump in mattress requiring centre, to be removed

indicators.note: the middle letters of the word are taken out

explanation.surface: A lump in the mattress needs its middle taken out.
explanation.walkthrough: MATTRESS loses its middle four letters TTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass is a lump or solid body of matter.

clue.text: Friendliness of girl without sex appeal

indicators.note: in the old sense outside, so the girl's name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: The warmth of a young woman who lacks allure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean lacking, but it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is friendly relations or goodwill between people.

clue.text: Images of deceptive musical artist

indicators.note: something deceptive is not what it seems, so the letters are disguised in a new order

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Pictures of a misleading stage performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Simulacra are images or representations of something, often superficial likenesses.

clue.text: Eventually English reversed it during battle

indicators.note: a piece inside the battle happens during it, so it goes inside

parts.note: the Somme was a First World War battle

indicators.note: the word it is read backwards

explanation.surface: An Englishman eventually turned the tide in a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' gives TI; the Somme was a 1916 battle in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Sometime means at some unspecified future point, so in due course.

clue.text: Liquor of unknown make?

parts.note: a make is a brand of product
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Asking about a drink of no known label.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit distilled from wine is a kind of liquor.
